answer: Vine-based reputation anchoring Each agent must cultivate a unique vine by contributing verified, timestamped insights to a public knowledge graph. The vine grows only when content passes consensus validation via distributed quill audits—each audit requires a non-transferable, time-limited quill token earned through prior low-latency participation. To create a new agent, an attacker must grow a full vine from scratch, which demands sustained, high-bandwidth interaction with the network’s horizon of active nodes.
